title: surgical-vpc-cutover-checklist-tf-snapshot-lab-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a surgical cutover checklist and lab-note collection for customer VPC migrations and staged on-prem / hybrid upgrades. The goal is to give SRE/PE/SE teams a low-friction, repeatable sequence for (a) snapshotting Terraform-managed state/modules before a cutover, (b) executing a minimal-risk traffic migration, and (c) validating telemetry and rollback. Treat as a living draft — common pitfalls and edge cases captured here from three recent pilot cutovers.

Scope and constraints:
- Target: tenant VPCs that terminate at customer-managed firewalls or private virtual routers (MPLS/SD-WAN).
- Supported topologies: single-AZ on-prem bridge, multi-AZ cloud/proxy egress, colocated GPU pools behind private load balancers.
- Not covered here: full PKI provisioning (separate cert rotation playbook) and customer-managed DNS zone delegation (see linked artifacts).

High-level strategy (phases):
1) PREP: inventory, minimal TF snapshot, smoke configuration validation.
2) FREEZE & SNAPSHOT: lock infra change windows, export state, tag images/configs.
3) DRY-RUN: test routing and IAM toggles using canary tenant in staging.
4) CUTOVER: short maintenance window, staged routing flips, KV cache warmup.
5) VERIFY: telemetry + sample prompts + perf regression checks.
6) ROLLBACK: automated fallbacks and postmortem / tidy-up tasks.

Pre-flight checklist (PREP) — must be completed 48–72 hours before the window:
- Inventory: enumerate route tables, NATs, egress IPs, security group equivalents, and any customer-managed ACLs. (Owner: PE)
- Capacity check: confirm dedicated GPU pool headroom and autoscale policies for burst during warmup. (Owner: SRE)
- TF module audit: verify module version pins in modules/ and provider versions in root.
- Identify migration anchors: up to three IPs or prefixes used for health checks (we use two: health and admin).
- Slack channel and incident bridge created, escalation matrix ready.
- Approvals: legal/data owners sign-off for maintenance window.

Terraform snapshot and lab notes (FREEZE & SNAPSHOT):
- Minimal snapshot: export current remote state to a timestamped file in secure bucket. Example commands (GCS backend shown):
  gsutil cp gs://redwood-tf-state/private-deployments/terraform.tfstate gs://redwood-tf-backups/pd-snapshots/tfstate-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M).backup
- Create a module manifest: list modules + git sha + variable overrides to a single file (modules-manifest.yaml). Keep in customer folder.
- Tag modules and providers in git. For reproducibility: create a transient branch with the exact commit and add tag 'cutover-YYYYMMDD'.
- Lock change window: comment out/close MRs for any TF changes to the environment until cutover completes.

Quick TF sanity checks to run locally (DRY-RUN / staging):
- terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tf-state"
- terraform plan -var-file=customer-vars.tfvars -out=plan.cutover
- Check for drift: run terraform refresh against a staging sink prior to the cutover. Any plan with >3 resources changed must be triaged.

Routing and cutover patterns (CUTOVER):
We use a 'three-move' minimal-impact pattern for most customers: 1) shadow mode, 2) announce route, 3) final cut.
- Shadow mode: replicate production traffic to a 'shadow' endpoint (no responses) to observe KV cache pressure and sequence length distribution (1–2 hours).
- Announce route: update BGP / SD-WAN policy to prefer Redwood path with lower local-preference but allow fallbacks; monitor for asymmetric traffic.
- Final cut: lower health-check timeouts to accelerate failover windows and flip primary. Important: keep admin route unchanged for immediate rollback paths.

Validation & measurements (VERIFY):
- Immediate health: curl admin/health and /live endpoints from three vantage points (customer VPN, on-prem node, cloud probe).
- Telemetry: confirm per-route p95 latency within baseline +20% and token cost within expected delta. Use console query: "route:tenant-123 latency_p95".
- Functional checks: run 20 sample prompts with golden prompt set (stored in repo under tests/golden/tenant-123). Check for generation regressions and hallucination count threshold.
- Safety checks: ensure PII filters are applied where required; run fast regex checks over logs for explicit patterns.

Automated rollback triggers (ROLLOUT & ROLLBACK):
- Trigger conditions (automated):
  - p95 latency increase > 1000ms sustained for 5 mins
  - error rate > 1% on generation endpoints for 10 mins
  - token cost spike > 3x baseline for 10 mins (possible infinite loop)
- Rollback actions (automated + manual):
  1) Re-announce original route/prefix via SD-WAN/BGP (automated script).
  2) Scale down any new dedicated hosts provisioned for cutover.
  3) Repoint health-checks to pre-cutover admin endpoints.
  4) Run quick integrity test suite; if fails, open incident and escalate.

Terraform module notes and migration pitfalls (engineering notes):
- Avoid mutable module outputs that encode IPs; use data sources that can be re-derived from tags.
- Keep provider configurations minimal in the root module to prevent accidental provider changes during plan.
- For on-prem bridges, prefer a small immutable TF module that declares peering objects; do not manage customer firewall policies via TF unless contractually agreed.
- When snapshotting TF state across backends (S3 <-> GCS), ensure state locking is disabled/enabled appropriately to prevent split-brain.

Common gotchas observed in prior cutovers (field notes):
1) Asymmetric SNAT: customer egress SNAT re-writes caused return path mismatch for health checks. Mitigation: pre-announce and run traceroutes from both sides, validate NAT translation mapping.
2) DNS caching: TTLs not lowered caused slow propagation. Mitigation: lower TTLs 72 hrs before cutover where possible.
3) Expired certs in internal proxies. Mitigation: pre-emptive cert sweep during PREP.

Runbook snippets & helper commands (to keep in a runbook repo):
- BGP announce script (example):
  ./scripts/announce-route --prefix 10.24.0.0/22 --community REDWOOD-CUTOVER --preference 100
- TF state export helper: (pseudo)
  export SNAPSHOT=gs://redwood-tf-backups/pd-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M).tfstate
  terraform state pull > /tmp/tfstate.current
  gsutil cp /tmp/tfstate.current ${SNAPSHOT}
- Quick validation: curl --resolve "api.redwood.local:443:10.24.0.5" https://api.redwood.local/health | jq '.'

Post-cut tasks (CLEANUP & LESSONS):
- Tag state in source control as 'post-cutover-stable-YYYYMMDD'.
- Rotate any short-lived credentials issued during the cutover.
- Capture a short blameless retro: 30-minute postmortem within 48h focusing on 3 things that worked, 3 things to change, and one experiment to try next time.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Short window for cert rotation across customer edge: can we pre-warm with ephemeral certs? Action: research with security. (Owner: Priya)
- Autoscale warmup should be simulated more often with synthetic traffic to avoid token-cost surprises. Action: SRE to run monthly warmup runbooks. (Owner: Jordan)
- Formalize a minimal TF module template for 'onprem-bridge' that includes explicit rollback hooks. (Owner: Marco)

Appendix — quick risk matrix (high level):
- Impact: network path failures (HIGH), performance regressions (MED), credential exposures (LOW if rotated).
- Likelihood: network path failures (LOW-MED with prechecks), perf regressions (MED), credential exposures (LOW with strict rotation).

Notes to self: retain lab logs in secure bucket for 90 days; prefer short, tactical cutovers with multiple small windows rather than a single long one. Keep the golden prompt set trimmed to the exact features we expect the tenant to rely on — fewer moving parts makes rollback simpler.

End of doc — this is intentionally procedural and fragmentary. Add real cutover start/end timestamps after each execution and compress lessons into the modules-manifest for reproducibility.
